market_holds: Spot $6.125 (sealed baseline 2026-11-23 18:08 UTC). It is down 50.5% from the $12.37 close on the day of the Q2 print (2026-08-19), 29.4% over 20 sessions and 10.8% over 5. It fell 35.8% from $8.52 (11-11) to $5.47 (11-20), then rebounded 12.2% on 11-23. My Yahoo bars put peers alongside: GDS -41.1% and VNET -37.5% over 11-11 to 11-20, then +13.4% and +18.3% on 11-23. KWEB was about -12% from its 11-06 high. Reports tie the slide to the tape and the sector, not to company news: a US Commerce rule against Chinese firms leasing Nvidia compute in overseas data centres (effective 11-19), Nvidia's leadership crisis and a global AI sell-off (StockStory 11-16; SCMP and Standard HK, mid-November). Options in the baseline: front-expiry (12-18) straddle 18.78%, ATM IV 89%, event-implied move 5.32% after subtracting 20d realised vol of 84.8%. That realised figure is inflated by the crash, so the event move is understated. Skew is 14.4 vol points to puts, put/call OI 0.26, and the ATM spread is 29% of mid, so the chain is thin. Consensus per the Earnings Whispers preview (finviz, 2026-11-16): EPS -$0.04, revenue about $492.8M (RMB ~3.5bn, +42% y/y and about +14% q/q, the same q/q pace as Q2). Another EW page has about $508M. There is no formal guide. An unconfirmed July report (Jiemian, 2026-07-02) gives a FY26 revenue target of RMB 12.5-13.5bn. H1 was RMB 5.78bn, so H2 needs 6.7-7.7bn, about 3.4-3.9bn a quarter. Q4'25 (03-18) +15.7% / +12.7%. Q3'25 (about 11-19-2025; the date is uncertain) about -5% at the open and -0.6% at the close, on a revenue miss (RMB 2.48bn vs about 2.63bn expected). Short interest: unavailable.
view: KC trades on the AI-cloud top line: total revenue against the RMB ~3.5bn bar, AI gross billings (RMB 1.33bn in Q2, +82%) and the adjusted operating profit turn. Its last three prints each closed +12 to +17%. The stock has since halved, and nearly all of the last leg came with the sector and the tape (GDS and VNET fell by the same amount over the same days), not with anything KC said. KC-specific inputs since the last call are mostly constructive. Alibaba's September quarter (11-19) showed AI cloud revenue accelerating to +53% from +45%, with external customers +67%. Chinese clouds raised AI compute and storage prices 30-50% in March 2026. Xiaomi's GPU budget at KC was reported raised to RMB 10bn+ and an Alibaba 5-year lease signed (Jiemian, July). Management said enterprise delivery is second-half weighted with 'quite a strong pipeline'. Consensus asks only that Q2's +14% q/q pace hold. Against that, the same July report said GPU deliveries to Alibaba and Xiaomi were badly delayed (under a third of H1's Alibaba servers delivered), and management said in July it was holding back expansion while hardware prices were high, so Q3 revenue conversion may lag. Memory costs pressure margins. Cash fell to RMB 4.67bn against RMB 6.7bn of borrowings and a RMB 15bn capex plan, so financing or dilution risk hangs over every print. Above all, the sector is trading on chip access and AI-bubble fear rather than demand: Alibaba's strong cloud print on 11-19 did not stop BABA falling. VNET's maintained guide lifted the group 13-18% today, so some relief is already in the 6.125 price. I lean modestly up, because the drawdown is the tape's and the company's own inputs point at a clean top line, but I cannot see the line and the Q3'25 miss shows delivery timing can break it. No recommendation.
unpriced: Possibly the gap between the company's own trajectory and a price the sector tape cut in half. Nothing KC-specific came with the 36% slide from 11-11 to 11-20; the slide matched GDS and VNET and came with a US chip-access rule that mainly hits overseas leasing, not KC's domestic capacity. If Q3 revenue lands near RMB 3.5bn with AI billings still growing above 60% and the adjusted operating profit holding, the stock sits at a level its own numbers do not explain. That is a lean, not a demonstrated gap: the 11-23 rebound and options pricing tail risk already hold part of it.

recommendation.reason: The setup leans up: three straight post-print pops, a halving driven by the sector rather than KC news, and peer demand data (Alibaba AI cloud +53%, industry price rises) that supports the trend q/q revenue consensus needs. But the deciding line, Q3 revenue conversion, depends on GPU deliveries that were reported delayed in July. The sector has ignored good demand prints all month, and today's +12% rebound has already taken some of the relief, so my probability does not reach 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Revenue clearly under RMB ~3.45bn with AI billings growth slowing (delivery delays), or an equity or convertible raise announced alongside the results.

self_critique: The sector has been trading on chip access, regulation and AI-bubble sentiment, and it ignored Alibaba's strong cloud print on 11-19, so a clean KC print may not lift the stock either, and the 11-23 rebound may have used up the relief. The July report of badly delayed GPU deliveries, plus management holding back hardware purchases at high prices, makes a Q3 revenue shortfall against a consensus that assumes trend growth quite plausible; KC missed on exactly this in Q3'25. A heavily levered, cash-burning name could announce funding. The three-pop history was earned from a higher-expectation, rising-sentiment base and may say little about today. This case keeps me near 50 and is why I do not recommend.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition was the most useful step: setting KC beside GDS and VNET showed the halving was the tape's, which framed the bar. P7 kept me honest that the line (revenue conversion under GPU constraints) is invisible, and the evidence on its inputs points both ways, so no call.
